sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Tier-3/4 Server Rack Space Leasing and Bare-Metal Server Hosting

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaties
Luxembourg-United States double taxation avoidance agreement (1996)
Luxembourg-China double taxation avoidance agreement (1983, as amended)
Luxembourg-Germany double taxation avoidance agreement (1958, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Combined regime under the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016 introducing the SCSp), the amended Law of 12 November 2004 against money laundering and terrorist financing, the Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners, and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 28 February 2019 on the implementation of the Register of Beneficial Owners.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of commercial registration extract of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) in the general partner's jurisdiction or equivalent competent registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for countries party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961; otherwise full Consular Legalization by the competent Luxembourg embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or certificate of non-impediment for the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or relevant state authority in the general partner's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity card of each natural person UBO and individual limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent government authority of the individual's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; certifying notary attestation accepted as complementary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO and partner (utility bill or bank reference letter)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated credit institution holding the account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization where issued by a public authority; otherwise notarized certification with apostille and translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate bank reference letter confirming source of funds and anticipated transaction activity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or other supervised financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; in the case of an unsigned electronic bank letter, the original under seal with a certified signature shall be apostilled

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Up-to-date extract from the UBO register or equivalent ownership chart of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Designated UBO registry or corporate register of the general partner's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for the underlying corporate documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, general partners, limited partners and sanctioned counterparties against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the Luxembourg external affairs sanctions list, and the US OFAC SDN list. Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) must be identified under the amended Law of 12 November 2004, subject to enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and senior management approval. Continuous ongoing monitoring and event-driven re-screening at least once every 180 days is required, with permanent recording of screening results in the AML compliance file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online filing portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The trade/company name must be available and not contrary to Luxembourg public order or morality. Official filings in the RCS are made in French, but the company name may be expressed in a Latin-script language; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters. The name of an SCSp must contain either of the statutory suffixes 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An applicant may reserve a name with the LBR for a maximum of two years. An extension may be requested before expiration by filing a new reservation request, subject to the name being continuously free. Upon rejection, the applicant may file an administrative objection with the LBR within fifteen calendar days of notification, accompanied by legal arguments and evidence of availability. If the LBR confirms refusal, the applicant may further appeal to the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal, which has jurisdiction to review the legality of the refusal; decisions of the Administrative Tribunal may be appealed to the Administrative Court within two months of notification.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible to establish substantive Luxembourg tax residency for a data center colocation leasing business. A professional domiciliation address may be used solely for the benefit of statutory RCS registration during the initial filing, but the SCSp must have a physical office and operational substance in Luxembourg, aligned with its actual data center and server leasing activities. A purely virtual office would expose the entity to substance challenge by the Luxembourg tax administration and loss of treaty benefits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For a low-risk standard AML tier entity in the data center colocation sector, the risk of unannounced physical inspection by the Luxembourg tax administration during the first three years is estimated at 15%. The risk increases to approximately 35% after the entity has obtained an Article 295 tax certificate, claims tax treaty benefits, or files VAT reclaims, at which point substance verification becomes standard practice.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: LBR statutory name reservation application fee
RCS initial registration fee for a Société en Commandite Spéciale
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration fee under the Grand-Ducal Regulation on RCS fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the SCSp registration notice in the Luxembourg official electronic gazette (Recueil des Sociétés et Associations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication tariff of the official gazette

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial registration with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
Notarial deed and drafting fees for the SCSp partnership agreement (if notarial deed is required or adopted)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard SCSp formation; statutory notarial tariff where applicable

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization processing for foreign corporate and individual KYC documents (estimated five bundles)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority in the country of issuance and the Luxembourg embassy or consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing official schedule of the issuing/authenticating authority

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of foreign documents into French, German, or English for Luxembourg legal filings
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per page and sworn translator tariff

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 944-1 to 944-22 (Special Limited Partnership or SCSp); Law of 11 January 2019 establishing the Register of Commerce and Companies; Law of 18 December 2009 on the electronic filing of corporate documents
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS), electronic filing through the eJustice/LBR online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for RCS registration and the SCSp deed filed for inscription in the Register, with publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an SCSp; the capital is freely fixed in the partnership agreement, and no escrow account or bank certificate is required unless the deed itself imposes a contribution funding condition
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the SCSp accepts the partnership capital contributions as set out in its executed partnership agreement, and confirms the admission and capital subscription of each initial limited partner; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the SCSp be established at 12 Rue de l'Église, L-2453 Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the undersigned general partner appoints [Name] as authorised manager (gérant) with sole signatory authority, and [Name] as alternate manager, with powers to file statutory filings and open bank accounts; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the forms and electronic filing procedures be approved and any registration formalities delegated to the manager.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS online portal (rcs.lu / eJustice.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the RCS commercial register to confirm that the proposed SCSp name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing corporate or trade name. File the online name reservation request together with the proposed corporate name, business purpose and general partner details. Obtain the reservation confirmation with a reference number to be used in the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if filed by a corporate service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is rejected as confusingly similar, submit a modified name through the same portal or request an internal review with the RCS registration department, specifying the distinguishing element of the proposed name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary for notarial execution, or the partners themselves where the law permits private execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the SCSp deed containing the registered office, precise corporate purpose, identity of general and limited partners, contribution obligations, profit-sharing rules, management powers, assignment restrictions, meeting procedures and liquidation provisions. Execute the deed before a Luxembourg notary or, if a private deed is used, ensure that all signatures are authenticated by recognised e-signature means valid under Luxembourg law.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of the general and limited partners
Statement of subscribed capital and contribution schedule
Consent of the registered office holder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS later challenges the admissibility of a privately executed deed, cure the irregularity by notarising the deed or by filing a formal rectification deed with the same registry, prior to the RCS inscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS electronic filing desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed SCSp deed and all annexes through the eJustice/LBR filing interface. Pay the statutory registration fee online. The RCS will validate the file, assign the Luxembourg trade register number and arrange publication of a notice in the RESA official electronic gazette.
required_dossiers: Notarial copy if the deed was notarised
List of authorised managers with specimen signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or rectification request, respond within the prescribed deadline with a corrected deed or additional corporate documents; in the event of refusal, file an appeal against the registrar's decision before the competent Luxembourg court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic VAT registration form on MyGuichet.lu or at the AEDT business desk. State the principal activity using the Luxembourg NACE code 62.09 (other information technology and computer service activities) with a description of data center colocation and bare-metal hosting services. Obtain the Luxembourg VAT identification number and, where applicable, request an EORI customs code.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of the general partner and authorised manager
Description of activity and estimated annual turnover
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEDT asks for clarifications, provide an updated activity description and turnover projections within fifteen days; if the matter is not resolved, request a meeting with the relevant AEDT unit or submit a formal appeal under Luxembourg tax procedural rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS), Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp as an employer with the CCSS in order to hire staff, including the manager if remunerated through the entity. Submit the registration via MyGuichet.lu and obtain the employer social security number. Attach the payroll implementation date and indication of the first registered employees.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of the general partner and manager
Planned hiring date and payroll mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If social security registration is delayed or queried, supply a certified copy of the RCS excerpt and the manager appointment resolution, and request confirmation of the effective registration date in writing from the CCSS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate bank account opening and LEI registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed credit institution in Luxembourg and an accredited LEI issuing organisation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the SCSp's name, presenting the authenticated partnership deed, RCS excerpt and proof of the manager's signing authority. The bank will conduct client due diligence and beneficial ownership verification. After the account is active, obtain a Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) for the SCSp, which will be required for financial contracts and regulatory filings.
required_dossiers: AML/KYC pack: passport copies, proof of address, source of funds and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the financial institution or LEI issuer requests further KYC information, promptly provide certified corporate documents, an updated beneficial ownership organigram or source-of-fund evidence; if undue delay persists, the SCSp may apply to another licensed establishment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy – Directorate General for Industry, together with the competent municipality for construction and classified establishment permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Classified establishment operating permit (autorisation d'exploitation d'un établissement classé) and municipal building permit (permis de construire) for the data center facility

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category registration or full EIA report depending on installed electrical capacity, cooling system and back-up generators; a Tier 3/4 colocation data center with diesel generating units is normally subject to an environmental impact screening and may require a full EIA assessment under the Law of 10 March 2017 on environmental impact evaluation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with Luxembourg air emission limits for NOx and CO from back-up generators, wastewater discharge limits under the Grand-Ducal Regulation on water protection, EU F-Gas Regulation (EU) No 517/2014 for cooling refrigerants, and the Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU requirements insofar as applicable; generators must meet the BaT conclusions for energy efficiency and continuous emission monitoring.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance issued by the local fire brigade and the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), structural load inspection certificate from an approved civil engineering bureau, occupancy permit from the commune, and workplace health and safety verification under the Luxembourg Labour Code including emergency lighting, evacuation routes, electrical safety and worker exposure risk assessment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct income taxes (portal: impotsdirects.public.lu); Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT (portal: aed.public.lu); Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) for business registration and the national business number (portal: lbr.lu); single e-administration portal: guichet.lu / myguichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the SCSp (Société en Commandite Spéciale): (1) execute the partnership agreement (private deed permitted; notarial deed required only in the case of a public offering) and file it with the RCS through a Luxembourg-approved professional within one month of formation; (2) obtain the national business number (matricule / numéro d'identification) from the Luxembourg Business Registers, which serves as the SCSp's registration identifier for tax correspondence and is required for VAT enrolment; (3) lodge the VAT registration application with AEDT (form 102 or via MyGuichet.lu) before commencing taxable colocation/hosting supplies, attaching the RCS extract, the partnership agreement, identification of the general partner and responsible manager, and evidence of the Luxembourg establishment and bank account; (4) receive the Luxembourg VAT identification number in the format LU + 8 digits + check digit; (5) because the SCSp is fiscally transparent for direct taxes, no corporate income tax account is opened in the SCSp's own name, and each partner is taxed individually, with non-resident partners deriving Luxembourg-source income required to obtain an appropriate Luxembourg tax reference; (6) amend the RCS/AEDT registrations within 10 days of any change and, where the SCSp has no fixed establishment in Luxembourg, appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative for compliance purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - The SCSp is statutorily fiscally transparent for Luxembourg corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (MBT) and net wealth tax (NWT); profits are attributed to and taxed at the level of the general and limited partners according to their profit-sharing ratios. Luxembourg-resident corporate partners are subject to CIT and MBT on their allocated share; resident individual partners are subject to progressive income tax; non-resident partners are taxable only on Luxembourg-source income (for example, income attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment or Luxembourg immovable property). For VAT purposes, however, the SCSp is an independent taxable person and is entitled and obliged to register, invoice and deduct input VAT in its own name.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime; the transparency of the SCSp is statutory and cannot be excluded unilaterally. The following elections and filings are available where relevant: (a) the option to levy VAT on an otherwise exempt lease or supply of immovable property under Article 43(2) of the Luxembourg VAT Law, commonly used for data-centre premises, subject to AEDT notification and tenant qualification; (b) the VAT grouping ('assujetti unique') election for qualifying Luxembourg group entities, available from 1 January 2024; (c) the fiscal unity ('intégration fiscale') election for CIT/MBT purposes among Luxembourg-resident companies with a 95% or greater direct or indirect holding chain, not accessible to the transparent SCSp itself; and (d) targeted transparency and hybrid-mismatch disclosures and documentation under the DAC6 and ATAD 2 rules where the SCSp's classification differs between Luxembourg and a foreign investor jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / TVA - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée), governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law (Loi du 12 février 1979, as amended), implemented in accordance with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for non-established foreign taxable persons: any taxable supply in Luxembourg requires VAT registration from the first transaction. For Luxembourg-established businesses, the small-enterprise franchise exemption applies to annual turnover not exceeding EUR 35,000; once turnover exceeds EUR 35,000, or on voluntary surrender of the franchise, VAT registration becomes mandatory. For intra-Community distance sales and B2C telecommunications, broadcasting and electronic services supplied by a Luxembourg business to other Member States, the annual pan-EU cross-border distance-sales threshold of EUR 10,000 applies, below which supplies remain taxable in Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate any real-time continuous transaction control (CTC), digital stamping, or pre-clearance API requirement; invoice issuance remains paper/PDF-based, subject to the EU authenticity, integrity and legibility rules. Mandatory electronic invoicing applies only to public-supplier (B2G) invoices addressed to Luxembourg contracting authorities, which must be transmitted via the national e-invoicing system using a PEPPOL-compatible format (UBL/CII). For B2B, e-invoicing is voluntary; however, all VAT records must be maintained in a standard electronic audit environment (SAF-T-LU / eCDF accounting file and the statutory VAT register) and must be delivered to the AEDT on request without prior notice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% VAT rate applies to (i) the export of goods physically dispatched or transported from Luxembourg to a destination outside the European Union, subject to proof of exit; (ii) intra-Community supplies of goods to a taxable person in another Member State, subject to the customer's valid EU VAT number and ECSL listing; and (iii) certain services related to movable tangible property or non-EU 'use and enjoyment' scenarios where the customer is a non-taxable person and the effective use takes place outside the EU. For data-centre colocation and hosting services, the B2B place-of-supply rule (customer's establishment) normally removes Luxembourg VAT entirely, with the customer accounting for reverse charge, provided the customer's taxable status and establishment are properly documented. Caution: where the supply is characterised as a supply relating to Luxembourg immovable property (for example, dedicated rack-space leasing tied to a specific site), Luxembourg remains the place of supply, no zero-rating applies, and the standard 17% rate (or the exempt-lease regime with an option to tax) governs the transaction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic SAD lodged with Luxembourg Customs via the ECS/ICS system, containing the MRN number issued at exit);
Transport and exit evidence: Bill of Lading (sea), CMR consignment note (road), or air waybill (air);
Inward Remittance Certificate (for non-EU arm's length exports) or the corresponding SWIFT MT103 / ACH wire record evidencing receipt of the export proceeds;
Commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin and, where applicable, dual-use or other export licences;

For zero-rated cross-border B2B services: written confirmation of the customer's status and place of establishment, including the customer's valid EU VAT registration number or a foreign tax-residence certificate.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT exercises active audit scrutiny over zero-rated exports and reverse-charge claims: the exporter must hold complete proof of export on file at the time the VAT return is filed; otherwise the AEDT will re-tax the supply at the standard 17% rate with retrospective effect. Late tax is subject to default interest of 0.6% per month. Formal infringements, including missing declarations, missing evidence and defective record-keeping, attract fines from EUR 25 to EUR 5,000. In cases of deliberate misstatement or fraudulent zero-rating, fines may be imposed up to 200% of the evaded VAT, and criminal proceedings can lead to imprisonment of up to 5 years; the general partner and managing persons of the SCSp are jointly and severally liable for the tax, interest and penalties. VAT assessments remain subject to the Luxembourg statutory limitation period, generally 5 years, extended to 10 years in the case of intentional wrongdoing or fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem and in cooperation with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and the European Central Bank (ECB). The BCL is responsible for monetary stability, payment systems oversight, and external-balance-of-payments statistical reporting; the CSSF supervises credit institutions and compliance conduct.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a euro-area jurisdiction with fully convertible current and capital account transactions. Under EU Treaty Articles 63-65 and the Luxembourg law implementing capital movement liberalisation, there are no foreign exchange controls, no prior authorisation for capital inflow or outflow, and no restrictions on profit remittances or partnership distributions. Convertibility is effectively total for EUR and any freely tradable currency. The only practical requirements are ordinary AML/KYC verification, BCL transactional reporting under balance-of-payments rules, and tax compliance documentation where non-resident withholding or substance assessment applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. There is no statutory obligation in Luxembourg to surrender export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no central-bank claim over export receipts. A data-center colocation operator receiving cross-border rental or hosting payments in EUR or foreign currency may retain, convert, or use such funds freely. Resident entities are required to report cross-border payments for statistical purposes to the BCL when amounts exceed the applicable reporting threshold, using the standard external transactions declaration and appropriate purpose code; such reporting is informational, not a surrender mechanism.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. Established payment and e-money institutions (for example certain PSD2-licensed EMI platforms offering multi-currency IBANs) can provide ancillary euro and foreign-currency settlement, virtual accounts, and payment initiation services. However, under CSSF practice they are not acceptable as the sole treasury rail or as a primary escrow/capital holding bank for a Luxembourg SCSp engaged in commercial leasing. Legal constraints arise from the distinction between e-money safeguarding and bank deposits, the absence of a full banking licence, cross-border outsourcing restrictions, and heightened correspondent-bank due-diligence expectations. Such EMIs may be used only as a secondary collection tool for small operational flows, subject to the operator's liability, safeguarding limitations, and a positive due-diligence outcome by the Luxembourg mandated bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, Luxembourg commercial banks require natural-person presence or an equivalent high-assurance identity verification process for all authorised signatories, ultimate beneficial owners, and the general partner representative of the SCSp. Remote onboarding is possible in narrow circumstances only when the client and its principals hold certified eIDAS-qualified electronic signatures and agree to a video-identification interview accepted by the compliance department. For conservative tier-1 banks, a physical onboarding session at the bank's Luxembourg offices or at a Luxembourg notary/registered agent office remains the market norm for partnerships with pass-through tax classification. The SCSp is not itself automatically blocked from remote opening, but the practical viability of remote-only onboarding is Low-to-Medium; robust substance and source-of-wealth evidence materially improves the outcome.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex multi-layer SCSp ownership with non-resident limited partners, discretionary family vehicles, or nominee arrangements obscures the ultimate beneficial owner chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified partnership deed, full register of partners and interest percentages, UBO cascade declaration, constitutional documents of each intermediate entity, source-of-wealth statements, source-of-funds evidence, audited financial statements or valuations, and a legal cover letter from Luxembourg counsel explaining the commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through tax status of an SCSp may be viewed by correspondent banks or the Luxembourg bank's risk committee as a potential tax-transparency or BEPS red flag, particularly when cross-border investors derive income from Luxembourg data-center leasing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg tax counsel opinion on SCSp fiscal transparency and commercial purpose, CSSF and RCS regulatory filings, substance documentation, internal management accounts, expected distributions and tax flow models, tax residency statements for each partner, and the agreed transfer-pricing or lease-margin policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Data-center colocation clients located in non-EU or higher-risk jurisdictions raise sanctions, export-control, or disguised-revenue concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full client due-diligence file with sanctions, PEP, and adverse-media screening results; ISIC/NAICS business profile of each customer; executed colocation agreements, service invoices, and payment flow descriptions; export-control and dual-use classification assessment; legal opinion on embargoes, where relevant; and representation letter from the SCSp general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital contributions from third-party payers, family office clusters, or mixed-purpose accounts may appear inconsistent with the registered economic activity of the SCSp.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised capital-call notices; subscription agreements and limited-partner undertakings; direct-payment instruction from each investor's own bank account; consolidated bank statements for all source accounts; source-of-wealth pack comprising sale agreements, inheritance documents, dividends, or loan agreements; signed AML/KYC questionnaire; and a clear separation of capital contribution versus operational income treasury policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient economic substance in Luxembourg for an SCSp whose only commercial activity is leasing Tier-3/4 data-center rack space and bare-metal servers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial substance file with lease agreement for Luxembourg premises or enforceable sub-lease rights, employment contracts or SEPA payroll records for local directors and operational staff, management meeting minutes, business plan and profit projections, utility and telecommunication contracts, bank relationship reporting, and the BCL/CSSF substance questionnaire completed by the responsible local service provider.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All capital injections should be routed directly from the limited partner's own bank account to the SCSp's fully opened Luxembourg bank account using SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 pacs.008 credit transfer with a valid UETR. The beneficiary BIC/IBAN must exactly match the bank account file, and the remittance reference must include a clear capital-call identification number and the words 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' to avoid misclassification. For balance-of-payments reporting, the transaction must be assigned by the reporting bank to the direct-investment / equity-capital category in the BCL external transactions declaration. The SCSp should pre-notify the bank's relationship manager with the capital-call notice, the investor's identity and source-of-funds file, and confirmation that there will be no third-party aggregation; each investor must pay separately. Inbound cross-border wires above the bank's internal threshold may be placed in a temporary escrow/suspense account only if the bank has pre-agreed that treatment; otherwise the funds should remain in the main operating account pending reconciliation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For euro-denominated payments within the EU and EEA, use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer through the Luxembourg bank's TARGET2 access. For non-EUR or non-EEA trade settlements, use SWIFT MT103 with full beneficiary banking details, UETR tracking, and the relevant commercial invoice or lease reference in Fields 70 and 72. High-value procurement of servers, cooling systems, or electrical equipment may be settled through a commercial letter of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) issued by the Luxembourg bank in favour of a confirmed supplier, using the underlying purchase agreement and supplier performance terms. Subsidiary or recurring data-center lease receipts may be collected via direct debit under SEPA B2B Direct Debit from EU clients, while non-EU clients should initiate SWIFT MT103 or use an approved corporate payment API with same-day reconciliation. All correspondent clearing should use SWIFT gpi to ensure transparent end-to-end payment tracking and to satisfy the bank's AML monitoring obligations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards between EUR and USD or other freely convertible currencies, executed under an ISDA 2002 master agreement and credit support annex with a Luxembourg or EU-regulated counterparty, limited to the SCSp's documented commercial exposures.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for hedging underlying receivables or payables in a currency with legal or practical convertibility restrictions, provided the economic exposure is fully evidenced and the NDF is not speculative; settlement may be in EUR or USD.

Cross-currency swaps and cross-currency basis swaps to match USD-denominated colocation income or lease liabilities to the EUR functional currency, with tenors aligned to the underlying contracts and EMIR reporting obligations satisfied.
Vanilla EUR/USD or EUR/GBP currency options (European-style calls or puts), used strictly for downside protection while allowing upside participation in a hedged commercial transaction.

Short-dated FX swaps (swap de change) for temporary liquidity grid management between the SCSp's EUR, USD, and other transactional currencies, under limits approved by the treasury committee and with each leg documented under a money-market confirmation.

Exchange-traded EUR/USD futures or cleared forwards, subject to the SCSp being admitted as an eligible clearing client or professional counterparty, used only to hedge net forecast cash flows, with margin and collateral arrangements separately approved by the relationship bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Deposit (depot des comptes annuels) - conditional on loss of SCSp exemption
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (LBR - RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Where mandatory: accounts must be approved by partners within 6 months of fiscal year-end; deposit with RCS within 1 month after approval. For calendar-year SCSp: approval by 30 June, RCS deposit by 31 July (net 7-month outside limit).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal reminder by LBR; court-ordered injunction and fine up to EUR 5,000; persistent non-filing may trigger RCS radiation (administrative strike-off), loss of standing in commercial transactions, and personal liability of the General Partner for resulting damages.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO Annual Confirmation and Updated Beneficial-Ownership Declaration (declaration des beneficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs, Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR - RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Event-driven: file within 1 month of any transfer or change in beneficial ownership; mandatory annual register verification recommended before 31 March of each calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal and administrative sanctions under the UBO Law of 13 January 2019: fines from EUR 250 to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 6 months; RBE extracts blocked; financial institutions, notaries, and contracting counterparties will refuse to process transactions or capital calls on the SCSp.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Register Audit and Partnership Transfer Register Posting (audit annuel des registres statutaires)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered agent at the registered office; production on request to LBR - RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Immediate posting upon each transfer of partnership interests, change of manager, or amendment of the partnership agreement; full audit of all statutory registers by the registered agent annually by 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unposted transfers are ineffective against the SCSp and third parties; assigning partner may lose priority; General Partner and managers become personally liable for damages caused by register defects; forged or materially false register entries attract criminal penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The SCSp is not automatically subject to audit. Mandatory statutory audit by an approved professional (reviseur d'entreprises agree) applies only where the SCSp: (i) exceeds at least two of the three large-undertaking thresholds under the Law of 19 December 2002 as amended (balance-sheet total EUR 20,000,000; net turnover EUR 40,000,000; average headcount 250) for two consecutive financial years; (ii) offers debt securities to the public; or (iii) the partnership agreement expressly opts into audit. A voluntarily appointed commissaire aux comptes may be required by contractual lenders or investors.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 and the Plan Comptable Normalise (PCN); IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for statutory accounts where adopted by the SCSp or parent undertaking; bookkeeping and tax-basis accounts follow the Loi Generale des Impots (LIR) transparency rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg RBE filings are event-driven rather than annual: every transfer of partnership interests, change of Ultimate Beneficial Owner, or change of manager must be declared to the RBE within 1 month of the event. The registered agent conducts an annual verification of the RBE entry against the partnership ledger and issues a dated annual confirmation record. The UBO chain must be maintained down to each individual holding more than 25%; failure to update prevents capital calls, distributions, notarized transfers, and bank account operations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (Registre des associes) / partnership interest ledger
Register of Managers (Registre des gerants) with specimen signatures
Register of Transfers (Registre des transferts de parts sociales)
UBO Register / beneficial ownership documentation log

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 2,800 (EUR 1,000 - EUR 2,500) per year for registered office domiciliation, legal correspondence handling, and annual register maintenance by a Luxembourg registered agent for an SCSp.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 15,000 - USD 35,000 for a full statutory audit of a data-center-asset SCSp where thresholds are exceeded; USD 4,000 - USD 8,000 for voluntary agreed-upon-procedures or review engagements when no statutory audit is triggered.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined (Luxembourg City: 17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax; reduced to 15% CIT on the first €175,000). SCSp itself fiscally transparent — entity-level CIT nil; corporate partners taxed on allocable share.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No data-center-specific tax holiday. Available: 80% IP Box exemption (Art. 50bis LIR; not applicable to colocation rents); R&D super-deduction 25%–50%; investment tax credit 8%–14% of qualifying capex; €17,500 municipal business tax abatement; SCSp exempt from net wealth tax. Unlimited trading loss carryforward with no statutory expiry; no carryback.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 100 (Déclaration d'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) — mandatory e-filing via ACD/MyGuichet.lu professional space (matricule + eSpace).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end (e.g., FY2024 return due 31 Dec 2025); newly formed entities may receive an individual ACD deadline; extensions only with explicit ACD grant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Matricule fiscal, RCS number, legal form (SCSp), registered office, fiscal agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the SCSp's Luxembourg matricule and the responsible tax representative; non-resident partners need not appear individually here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the fiscal year (month/day/year).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the SCSp's accounting period; no modification for partner residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net colocation and bare-metal hosting turnover, operating expenses, depreciation, arm's-length rental income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All Luxembourg-source commercial profit must be included even where a foreign corporate partner is the principal.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Each partner's name, address, taxable share percentage and profit/loss allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners' allocable share reported; treaty protection claimed at partner level, not in the SCSp return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Elimination of non-deductible expenses (e.g., 50% of non-deductible interest, excess limitations) and add-back of tax-exempt items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign PEP/expense allocations must respect the OECD arm's-length standard; otherwise recharacterization risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Trade profit base, abatement, applicable communal coefficient (Luxembourg City 6.75%).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SCSp carries on a Luxembourg permanent business, ICC remains assessed even if all partners are non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net wealth computation; minimum net wealth tax only where relevant.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: SCSp: exempt from net wealth tax — leave blank.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, investment credits, advance payments and solidarity surcharge off-set.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners claim treaty credits on their own returns; not in the SCSp return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signed by the general partner or an authorized tax agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The tax representative holds a power of attorney and is jointly liable for the substance of the filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine €250–€2,500 per return; after a 30-day reminder the ACD issues an imposition d'office with an up-to-10% arbitrary-assessment surcharge; late payment interest 0.6% per month; criminal willful non-filing attracts a fine up to €25,000 and custodial measures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: SCSp annual allocation statement (ACD information return, transmitted electronically via MyGuichet — no standalone paper form).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filed concurrently with the corporate partner's Form 100 deadline — 31 December following the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name, residence, tax ID and LP/GP status of each partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Required for non-resident partners to establish treaty eligibility and to evidence no Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Contractual profit share ratios and any special allocations (carried interest, catch-up).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocations must reflect the SCSp agreement and substance; artificial split of data-center income to low-tax partners triggers GAAR.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reference to premises, employees, servers, decision-making and contracts in Luxembourg.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If colocation servers and staff sit in Luxembourg, a PE likely exists for non-resident partners; failure to file a Luxembourg return creates evasion risk.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Same sanctions as Form 100; additionally the RCS may withhold a clean residence certificate where the annual allocation statement is missing.
